claim: For pure qubit states, maximal Entanglement Distance does not by itself constrain the quantum Fisher information for a prescribed common phase generator. With \(J_z=\tfrac12\sum_{i=1}^N Z_i\), every even \(N\ge2\) has states with the same maximal value \(E_{\mathrm D}=N\) but endpoint QFI values \(F_Q=0\) and \(F_Q=N^2\): a tensor product of singlets gives the first and an \(N\)-qubit GHZ state gives the second. Already for \(N=2\), the maximally entangled family \((I\otimes R_y(\theta))|\Phi^+\rangle\) has \(E_{\mathrm D}=2\) for all \(\theta\) while \(F_Q[J_z]=2(1+\cos\theta)\), so the full allowed interval \([0,4]\) occurs at one fixed maximal Entanglement Distance. Thus the trace-over-local-directions QFI/Entanglement-Distance identity should not be read as a generator-specific certificate of Heisenberg scaling for a prescribed collective sensing Hamiltonian.

integrity.literature_comparison_residual_risk: A closely related caveat could appear in uninspected portions of the primary manuscript, although targeted database and web searches found no exact coverage.

scientific_limitations: The generator-specific statement is proved for the prescribed common-axis collective generator \(J_z=\tfrac12\sum_i Z_i\).
The result does not challenge the summed local-direction Entanglement-Distance/Fubini--Study trace identity.
Primary-paper comparison used the arXiv abstract and detailed section-level text; the primary PDF itself was not available during this check.
title: Maximal entanglement distance does not constrain fixed-axis collective QFI
